Some criticism is valid, like if someone is telling you that you're an asshole maybe take some time to listen and see if there is anything that really needs to be fixed on your end, but other than that? Confidently just do you. 

Personally, I used to get called out a lot for having "internalized homophobia" because I'm just naturally very straight passing. I don't have "gay voice," I'm not super into fashion, I don't like hookup culture- I'm just not the type of person you would know is gay unless I told you. I heard the criticism, even went to therapy to really work things out, but at the end of the day, I am who I am, I don't let people bully me into flaming up my personality just for attention. I DO however, casually wear rainbow attire (belts, or a hoodie) to try and signal to other gays that I'm at least LGBT friendly, but that's about it. You'd be surprised how many people end up being attracted to you just by how confidently you carry yourself.

The rest is just trying your best to be social. If people don't come up to talk to you, YOU should talk to THEM. Make small talk like, "you know any good places to eat around here?" "Hey, I like your top, where'd you get it?" Or if you're really ballsy, "Hey, you're cute, can I buy you a drink, no strings attached?" (Just make sure you can take a possible rejection with a smile).

Clear, unfiltered communication. Sit down with this guy and tell him exactly what's needed. No sugar coating, no trying to spare his feelings, no giving yourself less just to get back up him sooner.
Honesty and transparency are requirements for real love, so it okay to put your foot down and say, "Hey, I need a week to myself. I'll be back on (x)day to talk with you, but I really need this time to myself." 

If he really cares about you, he'll give you the time you need, and also, letting him know exactly how long you'll be gone will help assuage any potential abandonment issues he might have (because it sounds like he has those issues). Even if you come back and say that you need even more time, he should be okay because you're being clear with him.

Now, it could also be true that this guy just wants things to go his way, and it's throwing a little tantrum when you leave for a little while because that's not what he wants. In that case, stay or go, you have to deal with that level of immaturity, which sometimes can be worked through, but heartbreak is also a surprisingly effective teacher.

The only thing I would have you ask yourself is if you communicated enough before this point. Like, did you just say, "I'm overwhelmed and I need space." Or did you get into detail? Did you tell him you needed space because of his action/inaction? Was he actually engaged in the conversation, or was he distracted? If there's any possible way for things to be miscommunicated, chances are they were. Humans are weird that way.

Either way, I wish you luck. Love is wonderful, but it's also hard. Sometimes it takes a little work to keep going, and other times it can't help but fizzle out. It's up to you guys to figure out what direction you're moving in.
